function: GNN allocates transmit power among the beams of an LEO satellite to maximize the sum of achieved data rates under uneven traffic requirements (pp. 1-3).
system: LEO satellite (Starlink example, 1150 km) with uniform planar array NA = NZ = 49, codebook precoding, 19 cells, carrier 11.45 GHz, no RIS (pp. 1, 4).
method: GNN (interference-sum message passing) trained unsupervised with meta-learning, soft combination of per-task SGD updates; few-sample fine-tuning or zero-shot in unseen tasks (pp. 3-5).
data_channel: Custom simulator: free-space path loss, Rician fading, array response (p. 2); Starlink parameters (p. 4); synthetic traffic distributions (uniform, exponential, spatially correlated); no dataset.
test_conditions: Meta-training on 16 traffic distributions, testing on two unseen scenarios without samples; trained with 19 cells, tested with more cells, up to 127 (p. 5).
baselines: Learned: FNN policy of [9]. Non-learned: equal power allocation, WMMSE [13]; plus upper bound from the sum of rate requirements (p. 4).
metrics: Achievable average data rate per user versus rate requirement, number of cells, training iterations, and time; table of required, actual, full-buffer rates (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "The channel from the satellite to the i-th user is assumed to be Rician fading" (own simulator; 3GPP is cited only for codebook beamforming, not as a channel model)
q2_support: p. 5: "In the meta-training stage, 16 traffic distributions in Table II are used to train the GNN. Then, we test the GNN in two unseen scenarios."
q3_support: p. 4: "Since the resource allocation policy obtained with the DRL algorithm in [9] is represented by an FNN, we use FNN as one of the benchmarks."; p. 4: "GNN and FNN outperform EPA and WMMSE by up to 30%"
q4_support: p. 4: "Within each iteration, the GNN is trained with SGD by Nsgd = 5000 steps" (training budget only; no order of complexity, operations, parameter count, or runtime of the GNN is reported)
q5_support: p. 4: "We take a Starlink LEO satellite as an example to evaluate our power allocation policy [10]." (simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset)
notes: Included, area 6: a GNN trained with meta-learning allocates transmit power among LEO satellite beams, which is physical layer in satellite links. q1 is 0: the channel is the authors' own simulator (free-space path loss given by [14], Rician fading, planar array response from [15] to [17], Starlink parameters from [10]; pp. 2, 4); 3GPP appears only for the codebook-based beamforming approach [3] (p. 2), not as a channel model. q2 is 1: meta-training on 16 traffic distributions and zero-shot testing on two unseen scenarios (p. 5, Fig. 6), and a GNN trained with 19 cells tested with other numbers of cells (p. 5, Fig. 5). q3 is 1: the FNN of the DRL policy [9] is the learned baseline, EPA and WMMSE [13] are non-learned, all compared on the average data rate in Fig. 4; FNN is absent from Fig. 5 and Table III. q4 is 0: only layer dimensions (Table I) and training steps are given, and the remarks on execution time are qualitative (p. 1). q5 is 0: simulated data, no link.
